findings.title: Call to non-existent no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added in UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). UsernameForm, UsernamePasswordForm, and their superclasses define no no-argument overload, so this code does not compile and the services module cannot be built.

findings.title: Passkey conditional UI is now disabled for initial login where no user is set yet
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) requires user != null, and it gates fillContextForm() in authenticate() (line 115) and challenge(error, field) (line 137). On an initial UsernamePasswordForm login the context user is still null, including for discoverable-passkey login, so the WebAuthn challenge, RP ID and conditional-UI attributes are never put on the login form. This reverses the previous user==null behaviour instead of extending it to re-authentication, regressing first-login passkey authentication and removing passkeys from the form re-rendered after an initial-login error.
